full_support_proof.route: The Comment asserts, for every c>0 and every epsilon>0, that P[sum_{i=1}^{n} L_i >= cn] >= P[L_1 >= cn] >= e^{-epsilon n} for infinitely many n, where the L_i are i.i.d. with law nu; this first equivalence is asserted by the author, not derived. It then picks 2^{n} pairwise disjoint paths from level n to level 2n in the binary tree G, so that along at least one of them sum_{i=1}^{n} L_i >= cn with probability >= 1-(1-e^{-epsilon n})^{2^{n}} >= 1-exp(-e^{-epsilon n}2^{n}) -> 1; extends that path to the root o; takes S as the vertex set of the extended path from o to level 2n; and concludes |partial_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/cn approx 2/c. Since c can be arbitrarily large, Phi*_E(G_nu)=0 a.s.
full_support_proof.completeness: The author prints the whole chain from the tail hypothesis to the closing conclusion. Nothing in the argument is supplied by this reader. The one step the author asserts rather than derives - the passage from 'nu does not have an exponential tail' to the two displayed inequalities - is kept as asserted, and the reader's closing editorial note says so. The final display bounds |partial_E S| over sum_{e in E(S)} L_e while the definition of Phi*_E on physical p. 234 bounds |partial_E K| over |K|; the two normalizations are not identified, in the source or here.
